chain.label: Unpowered, aerodynamically balanced ailerons susceptible to ice-induced hinge moment reversal
chain.trigger: during some airflow separation conditions, unpowered aileron control systems can be susceptible to undesirable aileron hinge moment changes (including asymmetric hinge moment reversals) and subsequent uncommanded aileron deflections

chain.label: ATR failed to disclose known freezing-precipitation/hinge-moment behavior in AFM, FCOM and training
chain.trigger: ATR failed to completely disclose to operators, and incorporate in the ATR 72 airplane flight manual, flightcrew operating manual and flightcrew training programs, adequate information concerning previously known effects of freezing precipitation on the stability and control characteristics

caused_by.evidence: ATR recognized the reason for the aileron behavior in the previous incidents and determined that ice accumulation behind the deice boots, at an AOA sufficient to cause an airflow separation, would cause the ailerons to become unstable

chain.label: DGAC and FAA oversight and icing certification requirements inadequate for freezing rain/drizzle
chain.trigger: the French Directorate General for Civil Aviation's inadequate oversight of the ATR 42 and 72, and its failure to take the necessary corrective action to ensure continued airworthiness in icing conditions

chain.label: Flightcrew had no information or training on ice-induced hinge moment reversal or its recovery
chain.trigger: the crew of flight 4184 had no reason to expect that the icing conditions they were encountering would cause the sudden onset of an aileron hinge moment reversal, autopilot disconnect, and loss of aileron control

caused_by.evidence: ATR's knowledge of the aileron hinge moment behavior and the associated autopilot behavior of the ATR 42 in freezing rain conditions ... was not explicitly incorporated into the ATR airplane flight manuals, aircraft operations manuals or pilot training programs
the DGAC and FAA did not recommend or require ATR or its operators to include this information in the specific aircraft manuals or pilot training programs

chain.label: Ridge of ice accreted aft of the deice boots during 39-minute hold in supercooled large droplets
chain.trigger: while the airplane was in a holding pattern during which it intermittently encountered supercooled cloud and drizzle/rain drops, the size and water content of which exceeded those described in the icing certification envelope

chain.label: Descent speed exceeded the flaps-15 limit; flaps retracted to 0 and AOA increased through 5 degrees
chain.trigger: as the airplane was descending in a 15-degree right-wing-down (RWD) attitude at 186 KIAS, the sound of the flap overspeed warning was recorded on the CVR ... As the flaps began transitioning to the zero degree position, the AOA and pitch attitude began to increase

chain.label: Aileron hinge moment reversal; ailerons deflected uncommanded to full right-wing-down
chain.trigger: the ailerons rapidly deflected to 13.43 degrees RWD

caused_by.evidence: the ATR's unpowered, aerodynamically balanced aileron control system ... can be susceptible to undesirable aileron hinge moment changes
the loss of control, attributed to a sudden and unexpected aileron hinge moment reversal, that occurred after a ridge of ice accreted beyond the deice boots
As the airplane pitched nose up and the AOA increased through 5 degrees, the airflow in the area of the right aileron began to separate from the wing upper surface because of the ice ridge

chain.label: Autopilot disconnected when the aileron deflection rate exceeded its monitor limit
chain.trigger: The autopilot could not control the aileron deflection rate, which exceeded that allowed by the autopilot so the autopilot disconnected

caused_by.evidence: the ailerons rapidly deflected to 13.43 degrees RWD, the autopilot disconnected

chain.label: Rapid uncommanded right roll excursions through inverted and steep high-speed descent
chain.trigger: the airplane rolled rapidly to the right, at a rate in excess of 50 degrees per second

caused_by.evidence: as the AOA increased to more than 5 degrees, the airflow over the right aileron separated again, resulting in a second aileron hinge moment reversal and rapid RWD aileron deflection
Within 0.25 seconds of the autopilot disconnection, the ailerons fully deflected to the RWD position and the airplane rolled rapidly to the right

rapid, uncommanded rolls and sudden multiple onsets of even 60 pounds of control wheel force without any form of warning or pilot training for such unusual events would ... preclude the flightcrew from effecting a timely recovery

chain.label: Nose-up pullout at 375 KIAS produced load factor exceeding 3.7 G
chain.trigger: This elevator input combined with the high airspeed (about 115 KIAS over the certified maximum operating airspeed) resulted in excessive wing loading

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was descending through 1,700 feet ... the elevator position and vertical acceleration began to increase rapidly
the AMR Eagle pilot training program did not include an 'unusual attitude' or 'advanced maneuvers' segment

chain.label: Outboard wing sections and horizontal stabilizer separated in flight near the ground
chain.trigger: the outboard portion of both wings and the horizontal tail separated in flight, in close proximity to the ground. The structural separation was due to excessive aerodynamic loads

caused_by.evidence: excessive wing loading and the structural failure of the outboard sections of the wings

chain.label: Airplane struck a soybean field nose down, partially inverted, and was destroyed
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted a wet soybean field partially inverted, in a nose down, left-wing-low attitude

caused_by.evidence: crashed during a rapid descent after an uncommanded roll excursion
the outboard 10 feet of the left and right wings, as well as the horizontal stabilizer, separated from the airframe at a very low altitude

chain.label: All 68 occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: the captain, first officer, 2 flight attendants and 64 passengers received fatal injuries

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable because the impact forces exceeded human tolerances, and no occupiable space remained intact
